fullPassage:
I became a book artist almost by accident. After graduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that time, I didn't think about working with books. Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book with beautiful notes written in it. That got me interested in the way paper was used in art. Soon after I returned to the UK, my father passed away. Feeling sad, I found myself picking up the Graham Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and cutting paper moths out of the pages. I then hung them over the open book. Since then, I have created sculptures out of books.
I always read the story first to get inspiration, and everything for the sculpture is made from the pages within that book; some don't have illustrations, so I take inspiration from the title and the text. I am also drawn toward fairy tales, especially Hans Christian Andersen's; his tales are quite magical, but there's also a sadness as they don't always have a happy ending.
For me, books are not only sources of ideas and associations, but also objects of great beauty to be cut up and rearranged. I use very simple tools: a sharp knife, a bit of glue, and some wire. Utilizing the open book as my base, I cut its pages, glue them, gently pull them up, and support them with wire. Through these processes, I construct physical representations of the narratives and the characters.

det.analysis: 'to be cut up and rearranged' — to be + 과거분사(수동태 부정사). cut up과 병렬구조로 rearranged.
det.tip: rearrange(재배열하다) → rearranged(재배열된) / to be + p.p. 수동태 부정사 병렬

ch: 필자가 태국에서 책 조각 기법을 배웠기 때문에
필자의 아버지가 책 예술가였기 때문에
필자가 대학에서 종이 공예를 전공했기 때문에
방콕에서 발견한 중고책이 종이 예술에 대한 관심을 불러일으켰기 때문에
questions.passage: I became a book artist almost by accident. After graduating in 2003, I traveled to Thailand. At that time, I didn't think about working with books. Shopping in Bangkok, I came across a used book with beautiful notes written in it. That got me interested in the way paper was used in art. Soon after I returned to the UK, my father passed away. Feeling sad, I found myself picking up the Graham Greene classic I had brought back from my trip and cutting paper moths out of the pages.
questions.stem: 필자가 책 예술가가 된 계기로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 방콕에서 발견한 중고책이 종이 예술에 대한 관심을 불러일으켰기 때문에.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 중고책→관심: 'came across a used book' + 'That got me interested in the way paper was used in art'
❌ ① 기법 배움: 태국에서 배우지 않음
❌ ② 아버지: 아버지는 돌아가심, 예술가 아님
❌ ③ 전공: 전공 언급 없음
det.tip: got me interested = 관심을 갖게 했다 / by accident = 우연히

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 영작하시오.

"나는 매우 간단한 도구를 사용한다."

조건: 5단어, use / very / simple 포함

det.korean: 나는 매우 간단한 도구를 사용한다.
det.analysis: I use very simple tools — 주어(I) + 동사(use) + 부사(very) + 형용사(simple) + 목적어(tools)
det.tip: simple tools = 간단한 도구 / very = 매우

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 영작하시오.

"나는 거의 우연히 책 예술가가 되었다."

조건: 8단어, became / artist / almost / accident 포함

det.korean: 나는 거의 우연히 책 예술가가 되었다.
det.analysis: I became a book artist almost by accident — became(~가 되었다) + by accident(우연히) + almost(거의)
det.tip: by accident = 우연히 / almost = 거의 / became = ~가 되었다
